content.text: how does this change behavior for the force migration?

I’ll check the migration path quickly so I’m not hand-waving here. The key question is whether `migrate --checkpoints v2 --force` pushes through this same `pushV2Refs` hook path or just rewrites local v2 refs.

For `entire migrate --checkpoints v2 --force` itself: no change. The migration still rewrites local v2 refs by pruning existing v2 checkpoint entries and re-copying from v1.

The behavior change is only when those v2 refs are pushed afterward, via pre-push:

- All-success case stays terse:
  ```text
  [entire] Syncing and pushing v2 checkpoints...
  [entire] Pushing v2/main, v2/full/current, ...
  [entire] All v2 checkpoints pushed
  ```

- Partial-failure case now says what landed:
  ```text
  [entire] Successfully pushed v2/main
  [entire] Warning: couldn't sync v2/full/current: ...
  ```

So for force migration, if it updates a lot of v2 data and a later push only partially succeeds, the user can now tell which migrated refs actually made it to the remote. It still does not rollback successful refs, and it still avoids saying “All v2 checkpoints pushed” unless every attempted v2 ref succeeds.

Instead of pushing the refspecs one by one, we could generate a list of refspecs and have git do the heavy lifting for us instead of trying to parallelize the whole process:

```
refSpecs := []string{
        "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main",
        "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current",
        "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000002:refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000002",
  }
```
It looks like git supports multiple refspecs at once:
```
	args := []string{"push", "--no-verify", "--porcelain"}
	args = append(args, opts.ExtraArgs...)
	args = append(args, pushTarget)
	args = append(args, opts.RefSpecs...)
```

That’s a good simplification. I’ll switch the v2 path to one multi-refspec `git push --porcelain`, then only fall back to per-ref sync/retry for refs Git reports as failed. That keeps Git in charge of the normal push while preserving the named-ref failure output.
